calendar.event: Shortened post-Thanksgiving session on NYSE and Nasdaq
calendar.why: Thin volume; a renewed AI sell-off would show Wednesday's rebound was holiday-light buying rather than a floor. S&P and Nasdaq are on pace for weekly gains.

covers: NYSE Wed 25 Nov close (US markets shut Thu 26 Nov for Thanksgiving; Fri 27 Nov is a half-day)

developments.text: Markets now price a 25bp Fed hike in December and another in early 2027 after hot October core PCE and an upgraded Q3 GDP.
developments.title: Fed hike cycle

developments.text: AI-linked stocks drove a sharp sell-off in November after Nvidia's CEO turmoil and funding worries; Wednesday's late dip-buying pulled the Nasdaq 100 back from the brink of a bear market.
developments.title: AI-stock sell-off and rebound

developments.text: The US proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, the EU, Japan and India, mostly 15–20% and up to 35% for Vietnam; officials say they are months from taking effect and lower rates are on offer for trade deals.
developments.title: US Section 301 'overcapacity' tariffs

for_malaysia: Rates channel: a Fed that is hiking again keeps US yields well above Malaysia's, which pressures the ringgit and limits room for MGS yields to fall. Sentiment channel: Bursa tech and data-centre names tend to follow the US AI trade, so Wednesday's swings are the main thing to watch there.
gaps: Fed funds target: could not confirm the current upper bound from an allowed source this run.
Nasdaq and S&P point changes not stated in the source read.
2-year yield is approximate; CNBC updates gave 4.588% and about 4.65% at different times.
Reuters, AP, WSJ and FT could not be reached from this session, so figures rest on CNBC and Bloomberg only.
headline: Wall Street erased most of a deep AI-led sell-off on Wednesday, then shut for Thanksgiving, with a hot inflation print locking in bets on a December Fed hike.
numbers_note: Only the intraday swing passed the filter: a 3%+ drop in the S&P 500 that reversed to -0.25% is a big reversal, while the closing moves, the 3bp drop in the 10-year and WTI's 2% gain were all inside the filter.

points.text: The S&P 500 fell as much as 3.2% and the Nasdaq as much as 4.6% on Wednesday before recovering; the S&P closed down 0.25% at 7,182.78, the Nasdaq down 0.62% at 23,585.80, and the Dow up 0.33% at 50,182.95. CNBC said no specific catalyst for the bounce could be pinpointed, though traders cited light pre-holiday trading and a Michael Burry blog post.
Tech fell as the lift from Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO faded and failed to calm worries about whether the AI trade can last.

October PCE inflation rose to 3.8% a year from 3.7%, and core PCE was 3.3%, slightly above the 3.2% forecast. Yet the 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 3bp to about 4.87% as investors bought bonds for protection.
Hotter core inflation, an upward revision to Q3 GDP and a Fed survey showing sticky inflation cemented expectations of a 25bp Fed hike in December and another in early 2027.
The White House proposed new 'overcapacity' tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, the EU and India; officials say they are months away from taking effect.
